A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Collaborative Threshold Watermarking by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification experiments on watermark fidelity, scalability, and removal attacks, plus simulated dealer-free setup timings in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds non-IID CIFAR-100 experiments and GPT-2 Small fine-tuning results on WikiText-2.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a weighted-FedAvg adaptation that divides embedding shares by public aggregation weights to preserve the watermark direction. This changes the embedding procedure for weighted aggregation; the existing setup, uniform-aggregation algorithm, and verification procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's IID image-classification coverage, v2 evaluates CIFAR-100 with heterogeneous client label distributions and adds language modeling through GPT-2 Small fine-tuning on WikiText-2. These introduce a distinct federated data scenario and a new task domain.

E2.justification: The independent per-client watermark baseline in Figure 3 is unchanged. The new experiments use unwatermarked controls, extending an existing comparison type without adding competing watermarking methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds a balanced Dirichlet sweep with four concentration values and a language-model protocol using four clients, 20 rounds, AdamW at 0.0001, perplexity, and minimum-perplexity checkpoint selection. Appendix D.2 also replaces the estimated-key L1 penalty with absolute cosine alignment against model parameters. This is a reported attack-protocol revision; unchanged plots do not establish rerunning it.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 tests sensitivity to client label heterogeneity at fixed K = 32 and c = 0.025. Appendix D.2 revises the existing adaptive-attack formulation, while the extensive original attack analyses and their plotted outcomes are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three seeds, 0, 1, and 2, retain the existing uncertainty summaries, and identify Figure 10 error bars as 95% confidence intervals. The new tables extend existing reporting practices without introducing additional runs or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports non-IID z-scores of 12.58–12.72 and watermarked accuracy reductions of 0.16–0.53 percentage points. New Table 3 reports watermarked perplexities of 10.58–10.70 versus 10.52 without watermarking, with z-scores of 6.89–9.63. These substantively extend findings to new settings; existing Table 1 and result figures remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 introduces positive normalized aggregation weights, defines reciprocal-weighted embedding shares, and derives the cancellation identity preserving their aggregate direction in Equations 8–9. Existing secret-sharing arguments, verification mathematics, and dealer-free complexity analysis are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the empirical applicability claims to non-IID partitions and language-model fine-tuning. The central threshold-watermarking contribution, scalability claim, and original removal-robustness claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added experiments as showing limited sensitivity to label heterogeneity and applicability beyond image classification. Section 6 replaces the IID-only, image-only limitation with a narrower qualification that comprehensive evaluation of larger language models remains future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link in the abstract and documents the balanced Dirichlet partition and language-model training settings in Appendix C. Existing image preprocessing, hardware, and training details are retained. The PDFs establish the new access statement, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds Radford et al. (2019) for GPT-2 and Merity et al. (2017) for WikiText-2. Section 7 and the claimed relationship to earlier watermarking methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the method overview, inserts two experimental subsections, rewrites the adaptive-attack explanation and limitations, and replaces placeholder correspondence and preprint information. The overall section structure and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds result Tables 2–3 and expands the notation table, renumbered from Table 2 to Table 4. Figures and algorithm floats shift with the surrounding text, but all twelve existing figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v2 partly addresses v1's explicit IID-only and image-only limitations with relevant new evidence, adds weighted-aggregation support, and makes the documented adaptive-attack penalty consistent with reducing alignment. The gains are bounded: language-model evidence covers detection and fidelity in one small-model setting, and unchanged attack plots do not establish renewed validation of the revised loss. Overall, the paper becomes more complete without substantially strengthening its central robustness evidence.
